_what: Purity and oligonucleotide-identity characterisation recovered from the Quality/CMC sections of regulatory documents ALREADY HELD in sources/documents/. Phase 2 requires the dataset to carry 'data on the purity and characterization of each' oligo and the methodology document to state 'the methods used to purify and characterize oligo identity'; this dataset reported purity for 0 of 218 compounds because earlier extraction read only the clinical sections of these same files.
_method: 11 parallel extraction agents, one per compound programme, each reading only its own documents, followed by 11 adversarial verification agents that string-searched every quote against the cited file and checked every numeric purity against a printed purity context. 8 groups verified clean; 3 reported defects, all of which were metadata errors rather than bad values, and all are corrected in this file with the correction recorded in the record.
_caveats: A public EPAR names the analytical method and withholds the numeric acceptance limit: that is recorded as purity_limits_redacted=TRUE with purity_pct NOT_REPORTED, never as a value. A drug-substance SPECIFICATION is not the tested batch of any particular study; purity_pct_basis says which it is and a specification is never spread across batches.

records.characterisation_methods: Sodium content by Flame AAS; water content by Karl Fischer (KF); elemental impurities by ICP-MS; residual solvents by GC; assay by UV; pH (Ph. records.purification_method: Eight-step active-substance process: conventional solid-phase synthesis of each single strand (Step 1), cleavage and deprotection (Step 2), crude ultrafiltration (CUF, Step 3), purification by anion exchange (Step 4), second ultrafiltration (Step 5), annealing of the two strands to form the duplex (Step 6), concentration (Step 7), lyophilisation and packaging (Step 8). records.purity_method: Purity and impurities by LC-UV-MS, as listed in the active substance specification. (Related characterisation at 2.4.1.1 identifies the chromatographic mode as ion-pair high performance liquid chromatography.)

records.impurity_classes: Impurities classified into organic impurities, inorganic impurities and residual solvents. Organic impurities sub-classified into process-related impurities, impurities derived from starting materials and reagents, and potential degradation products, grouped by structure and formation mechanism with toxicological qualification of the impurity groups. Also discussed: small molecule impurities, impurities with genotoxic potential, nitrosamines, and elemental impurities. Omission of routine residual solvents and elemental impurities testing was justified (elemental impurities below the control threshold); a nitrosamine risk assessment concluded no risk in the drug substance and no confirmatory testing was performed.
records.purification_method: Synthetic oligonucleotide manufactured at one site in a 7-step process from well defined starting materials: solid phase synthesis on an oligonucleotide synthesizer, cleavage of the oligonucleotide from the solid support, removal of the amide protecting groups from the nucleobases, then purification steps; finally filtered through a sterilisation grade filter, dispensed and stored in sterile single-use flexible bioprocess bags (LDPE contact layer) protected from light. The lyophilisation step was eliminated and the active substance is supplied as a solution. (2.4.1.2. Manufacture, process controls and characterisation.)
